summary: Streaming chat endpoint returns generic 500 instead of standardized residency policy violation error (should be 409 + error_code)
environment: prod (customer base_url set to us-east while org is pinned to EU-only)
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer enabled EU-only region pinning for Hosted API.
- Non-streaming requests correctly return the new residency enforcement error contract (HTTP 409 + machine-readable code).
- Streaming requests (SSE) to the same endpoint return a generic HTTP 500 with "internal server error" and no residency error_code.

Impact:
- Breaks client-side handling and retry logic (SDK treats 500 as transient, but this should be a deterministic policy block).
- Causes confusion for customer security/compliance teams during validation.

Expected behavior (per ADR-022):
- When region pinning blocks a request, return:
  - HTTP status: 409
  - error.code: residency_policy_violation
  - include request_id; include help_url; do NOT leak sensitive policy internals.

Actual behavior:
- Streaming path returns:
  - HTTP status: 500
  - payload: {"error":"internal_server_error"} (or empty body depending on client)

Repro steps (Support validated):
1) Use an org/project with residency policy set to EU-only (primary: eu-west).
2) Send request to us-east base URL.
3) Compare behavior between non-streaming and streaming.

Repro curl:
- Non-streaming (correct):
  curl -i https://api.us-east.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'

- Streaming (incorrect):
  curl -i -N https://api.us-east.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'

Observed logs (from customer + support replay):
- request_id: req_01HSX6T7J9J4C3A8G7V9E2ZQK8
- gateway status: 500 (stream)
- router decision (downstream): block_reason=residency_region_not_allowed; allowed_regions=[eu-west]; requested_region=us-east

Notes:
- This appears limited to the streaming handler/proxy path; enforcement decision is happening but the gateway is not mapping it to the public error contract when stream=true.
comments: 2025-02-21 09:18 UTC - Hannah Schmitt (Reporter): Customer reports SSE stream requests return 500 after enabling EU-only pinning. Non-stream requests return the expected 409 + residency_policy_violation. Attaching request_id req_01HSX6T7J9J4C3A8G7V9E2ZQK8 and curl repro from customer.

2025-02-21 10:02 UTC - Avery Johnson: Confirmed on our side using staging + forced policy. Streaming path returns 500 with no structured error. Non-streaming returns 409 as expected. Escalating to API Gateway (Amara) + error contract owner (Brian).

2025-02-21 11:11 UTC - Amara Diallo: Triage: streaming endpoint uses a separate code path (SSE proxy) and currently wraps upstream non-2xx into a generic 500 to avoid partial streams. If policy evaluation happens after stream plumbing starts, we lose the original status/code. Investigating where enforcement is invoked for stream=true.

2025-02-21 13:40 UTC - Brian Murphy: Per ADR-022 we must return deterministic 409 before streaming begins. Even if the client asked for stream, a residency block is pre-flight and must not downgrade to 500. Suggest mapping the router/gateway error type directly to the standard error payload and ensuring headers/status are written prior to any SSE bytes.

2025-02-22 08:25 UTC - Amara Diallo: Found root cause: the streaming handler calls the routing service via a "streamProxy" wrapper that treats any non-200 from routing as an internal proxy error and rewrites to 500. The routing service is already returning a structured policy block (409 + error_code), but we drop it. Fix in progress to preserve status and emit the standard error payload (non-SSE) when blocked pre-stream.

2025-02-23 16:10 UTC - Amara Diallo: Fix merged to main in redwood/pr-21533 (adds deterministic enforcement response + standardized error payload across streaming/non-streaming). Added unit coverage for stream=true path; E2E coverage tracked in ENG-4851.

2025-02-24 12:55 UTC - Sean Gallagher: Deployment plan: rolling out gateway patch to prod us-east then eu-west. Monitoring 5xx rate + residency blocks dashboard. No flag flip required; change is backwards compatible.
2025-02-25 09:05 UTC - Hannah Schmitt: Customer retested against us-east base_url with stream=true and now gets HTTP 409 with error.code=residency_policy_violation and help_url. Marking resolved.
root_cause: API Gateway streaming (SSE) proxy handler rewrote upstream policy-block responses into a generic 500. The residency enforcement decision was being returned correctly from routing, but the streaming wrapper treated any non-2xx as an internal proxy failure and discarded the public error contract fields.
resolution: Gateway fix deployed to production to preserve residency enforcement status/code for streaming requests and return the standardized error contract (HTTP 409 + error.code=residency_policy_violation + request_id/help_url) before any SSE bytes are written. Customer confirmed behavior on 2025-02-25.
workaround: Customer workaround prior to fix: use non-streaming requests for residency validation or point base_url to an allowed region endpoint (EU) to avoid policy blocks. Not recommended long-term as it breaks expected streaming behavior.
next_steps:
1) Ensure ENG-4851 E2E tests cover streaming residency blocks and CI gates it.
2) Add a gateway regression test asserting stream=true never downgrades deterministic policy errors to 5xx.
3) Update Support macros to request request_id + base_url + whether stream=true when triaging residency issues.
customer_communication: Shared explanation that this was a gateway bug in the streaming handler and not a misconfiguration; provided expected behavior (409 + residency_policy_violation) and confirmed fix deployment window. Customer confirmed resolution after rollout.
internal_notes: If this reappears, check whether any bytes were written to the response before the enforcement decision. If headers are committed, we cannot change status; must ensure residency enforcement is evaluated pre-stream in gateway for all streaming endpoints.
